messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- The product catalog is owned by the Atlas team as of 2025-12-19, having moved from Cinder. [decision; valid 2025-12-19 to now; recorded by handover/2025-12-19-catalog]
    earlier: Cinder owns the product catalog. [valid 2025-01-17 to 2025-12-19; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-01-17]
- The product catalog can be released on weekdays between 08:00 and 10:00 UTC, never on Fridays; the previous Mon-Thu 09:00-17:00 UTC window no longer applies. [constraint; valid 2025-09-03 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-09-03]
    earlier: The product catalog can be released on Mondays to Thursdays between 09:00 and 17:00 UTC; anything else needs an exception. [constraint; valid 2025-03-17 to 2025-09-03; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-03-17]
- As of 2025-12-19, the Atlas team is taking over the product catalog from the Cinder team. [decision; valid 2025-12-19 to now; recorded by handover/2025-12-19-catalog]
- On 2025-12-18 the Atlas team decided that the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every product catalog write, because incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes. [decision; valid 2025-12-18 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-12-18]
- On 2026-03-20 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change. [valid 2026-03-20 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-03-20-2]
- The indexer relies on the product catalog for product documents, so if the product catalog is down the indexer is down. [valid 2025-01-30 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-01-30]
- On 2026-02-16 the Dune team noticed that the product catalog's request volume halved after the client rollout and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-02-16 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2026-02-16]
- On 2026-06-04 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-06-04 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-06-04]
- Dashboards and alerts for the product catalog are being repointed as of the 2025-12-19 handover. [valid 2025-12-19 to now; recorded by handover/2025-12-19-catalog]
- The product catalog keeps image metadata in a separate table because the joined writes were locking product updates for seconds at a time. [valid 2025-04-17 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-04-17]
- As of 2025-08-25, the ledger service deploys on Wednesdays between 09:00 and 11:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-08-25 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-08-25]
- The product catalog will keep image metadata in a separate table. [decision; valid 2025-04-17 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-04-17]
- The image resizer is a hard dependency of the product catalog. [valid 2025-04-14 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-04-14]
- On 2026-05-27 the Atlas team noticed that the indexer's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-05-27 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-05-27]
- As of 2025-08-25, the ledger service only ships on Wednesdays between 09:00 and 11:00 UTC; the previous weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC slot is retired. [constraint; valid 2025-08-25 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-08-25]
    earlier: The ledger service only ships on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-01-14 to 2025-08-25; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-01-14]
- On 2025-12-25 the Atlas team noticed that the reports pipeline's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2025-12-25 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-12-25]
- As of 2025-12-29, the auth gateway deploys only on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-12-29 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-12-29]
- On 2025-10-15 the Atlas team noticed that the image resizer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners. [valid 2025-10-15 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-10-15]
- On 2026-04-16 the Atlas team noticed that the ledger service's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2026-04-16 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-04-16]
- As of 2025-09-02, most requests to the feature-flags service at peak were identical. [valid 2025-09-02 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-09-02]

Question: What is the availability target for the catalog?

message.reasoning: The question asks about the availability target for the catalog. Looking through the memory, I see entries about ownership, release windows, dependencies, disk usage, etc., but no availability target is mentioned anywhere.
